items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Freeman provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
notes: That the previous meeting minutes be approved.

items.title: Consent Motion
notes: That consent motion items (a) through (b) be approved.

items.title: Items Removed From the Consent Motion
2025 Sustainability and Climate Change
notes: Ena Ristic gave a presentation outlining the City’s contributions to sustainability and climate change, including key topics like the upcoming Earth Day and the commitment to active transportation. She then responded to questions of Council. Kevin Van Ooteghem also responded to questions of Council.

Kae Elgie, Resident of Waterloo gave a presentation encouraging the City to continue working on community greenhouse gas emission goals, and to encourage the community to take part in Jane’s Walks happening across the City. She then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Culture Plan Benchmarking Report
notes: Lakyn Barton gave a presentation highlighting the City’s work over the past year in celebrating local culture, as well as giving a snapshot of the past decade with the current Culture Plan. She then responded to questions of Council. Astero Kalogeropoulos and Justin McFadden also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: 2025 Business Improvement Area Levy
notes: Jeyas Balaskanthan, Executive Director, Uptown Waterloo Business Improvement Area gave a presentation highlighting the accomplishments of the Uptown BIA over the past year. He then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: 2025 Special Service Levy
notes: Councillor Hanmer having previously declared a pecuniary interest was absent for the taking of the vote.
Mayor McCabe having previously declared a pecuniary interest was absent for the taking of the vote.

items.title: Official Plan Amendment No. 63
notes: John Vos gave a presentation outlining the proposed development, providing an overview of the current Official Plan and Zoning By-law designations and the proposed amendments. He then responded to questions of Council.
Kristen Barisdale, GSP Group gave a presentation offering further details on the proposed development, including site context. She then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

items.title: Consideration of Notice of Motion Given at Previous Meeting
notes: Councillor Julie Wright – Support the Need for Provincial Action on Salt Pollution from Road Salt
Dani Lindamood, Campaigns & Communications Director, Water Watchers spoke in support of this motion, emphasizing the need for water protection.
Joe Salemi, Executive Director, Landscape Ontario spoke in support of this motion, providing information on the need for road salt management to reduce freshwater salt pollution.

motions.item_title: Consideration of Notice of Motion Given at Previous Meeting
motions.text: WHEREAS road salt is a known toxic substance designated under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act because of tangible threats of serious or irreversible environmental and health damage from road salt; and WHEREAS salt levels in Ontario’s groundwater aquifers, creeks, rivers, and lakes have increasingly worsened since the 1970s, seriously affecting municipal drinking water sources and aquatic life; and WHEREAS the City of Waterloo, in collaboration with the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, is actively attempting to mitigate salt pollution using existing policies, programs and site design measures that would be significantly more effective with supporting Provincial legislation; and WHEREAS the Ontario and Canadian governments have taken many actions over the past 25 years including setting water quality guidelines, developing voluntary codes of practice, signing the Canada-Ontario Great Lakes Agreement, and holding workshops, yet still the salt problem continues to grow; and WHEREAS numerous situation analyses have recommended salt solutions involving liability protection, contractor certification, government- approved Best Management Practices (BMPs) and salt management plans; and WHEREAS increased numbers of slips and falls claims, and other injury/collision claims related to snow and ice, are resulting in salt applicators overusing salt beyond levels considered best practices; and WHEREAS unlimited contractor liability is making it difficult or expensive for snow and ice management contractors to obtain insurance coverage, resulting in contractors leaving the business, thereby making it difficult for municipalities and private owners to find contractors; and WHEREAS the Snow and Ice Management Sector (SMS) of Landscape Ontario is working with the Ontario government to institute a limited liability regime for snow and ice management, including enforceable contractor training/certification and government-approved BMPs for salt application; and WHEREAS many Ontario municipalities have Salt Management Plans, but these often require updating considering improved science and better salt management practices now available. THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The City of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to work on a priority basis with key stakeholders to develop limited liability legislation, including enforceable contractor training and a single set of provincially-endorsed standard BMPs for snow and ice management; and 2. The City of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to create and fund an expert stakeholder advisory committee to advise the province and municipalities on the best courses of action to protect freshwater ecosystems and drinking water from the impacts of salt pollution; and 3. This resolution be sent to all municipalities in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), local MPPs, Conservation Ontario, Minister of the Environment Conservation and Parks (MECP), the Attorney General, and Premier Doug Ford.
